chapter_theme: Thiruvezhukutrirukkai (திருவெழுகூற்றிருக்கை): the closing number-poem, in which the numbers one to seven rise and fall through the lines while the praise tells Murugan's story: the one form of the Taraka Brahman, the release of Brahma, the circling of the world, the marriage to Devayanai, the teaching of Siva, the birth at Kazhumalam as master of three Tamils, the vel at Krauncha, and the lord of Eragam on the Kaveri's north bank.
structure_note: A single song in the form of the ezhukutrirukkai, where numbers are woven in ascending and descending order (ஒன்று, இரண்டு, மூன்று ... ஏழு and back); it is all praise, with no confession.

1326.reading: All praise, counted out in numbers: Murugan, the one form of the Taraka Brahman, born in the one line from the two and never ageing, once lifted Brahma's tuft in a blink and freed him from prison when the three gods begged at his feet, circled the four-fold sea-girt land in an instant on the two-winged peacock, married the daughter of the one-trunked, four-tusked elephant, became younger brother of the five-armed, arugu-wearing Ganesha, and guru to the three-eyed Siva who teaches the Vedas in the five letters. He was born at Kazhumalam, drinking Uma's milk, as the master of three Tamils and king of four kinds of poetry, born of six stars, split the Krauncha hill with one vel, and dwells as lord of Eragam, the hill on the Kaveri's north bank where Brahmins of the six letters praise his feet.
1326.nuance: The numbers carry the form, not the sense: the device is the classical ezhukutrirukkai, a chariot-shaped number poem. தாரகப் பிரமம், the 'saving Brahman', is the pranava, and Murugan's guruship over Siva (முக்கட் சுடரினை ... ஒருகுரு வாயினை) is set inside it. கழுமலத்து உதித்தனை ... முத்தமிழ் விரகன்: Murugan identified with Sambandar, born at Sirkazhi and fed by Uma. ஆறெழுத்து அந்தணர்: the six-letter mantra of Murugan. Some number-phrases (இருபிறப்பாளரின் ஒருவன், ஒருவகை வடிவினில் இருவகைத்தாகிய மும்மதன்) are obscure.

links.note: Tirumular's first verse counts the Lord from one to eight (one, two by grace, within three, knowing four, conquering five); 1326 uses the same counting device through seven to tell Murugan's acts, so the numbers become theology in one and narrative in the other.

source_issues: 1326: the number pattern is broken in places by run-together words (குடிமி for குடுமி, அன்றி லங்கிரியிருபிள வாக, காவிரிவடகரை ... குருகிரிஇருந்த), probably transcription spacing.
